summary_for_children: Ar-Rahman means The Most Merciful. It lists Allah's gifts: teaching the Quran, the sun and moon, the balance, fruits and grain, two seas with pearls and coral, and asks again and again which of His favours we would deny.
environment_concept: A world built as a series of balanced gardens and shores, each closing with the surah's refrain 'So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?', from the sun and moon in precise calculation to the two seas meeting with pearls and coral.
architecture_and_scenery: A sun-and-moon orrery over meadows, a great balance scale at the centre, palm and grain terraces with fragrant plants, a pottery-clay riverbank, and a coast where two seas meet with a barrier, ships with high sails on the horizon.

palette.lighting: Bright, balanced daylight shifting between two sunrises and two sunsets

activities.name: Keep the balance
activities.description: At the great balance, tap the pans to add or take away weights until it hangs level, then read 55:9.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Pearl and coral
activities.description: Find a pearl and a branch of coral in the shallows, from both waters.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Match each place to its ayah
activities.description: Match each favour in this world to the ayah it comes from; each ends with the refrain of 55:13.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Two sunrises
activities.description: Talk about how the sun rises at different points through the year.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Plant the garden
activities.description: Set four young plants in their labelled beds: fruit, palm trees, grain and scented plants.

narration_plan: Narration is gentle and rhythmic: each area ends with the refrain read in Arabic and meaning.

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A green coast where a river runs into the sea past a long pier with buoys, palm and fig gardens on the slopes

primary_mechanic.text: At each buoy along the pier, lower the testing tube and read the float: it rides higher in salt water than fresh. Record fresh or salt at every buoy (wrong answers are refused with the reason), then mark between which two buoys the waters meet (55:19-20).

secondary_activities: the Most Merciful taught the Quran (55:1-4, read)
fruit, palms and scented plants (55:10-13, read)
unique_world.narrative_structure: Three readings down the coast, the pier test, then a reading at the foot of the pier
world_assets: buoys that change colour when tested
environment_behaviour: tested buoys turn green (fresh) or blue (salt)
a line of floats appears where the waters meet
unique_world.learning_objective: Know the refrain of Ar-Rahman (55:13) and the sign of the two seas meeting (55:19-20)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The World of Blessings
story_library.children_narration: The sun, the moon, the trees, the seas, and the fruits around us are among the signs of Allah's blessings. Surah Ar-Rahman repeatedly invites us to recognize these gifts. It encourages gratitude and reflection.

world_idea.title: The Living Symphony of Nature
world_idea.description: Explore distinct biomes, observe fruit-bearing plants, discover the meeting of different bodies of water, and interact with educational models of natural balance. Depictions of Paradise must remain symbolic rather than claiming to show the unseen reality.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The library allows "symbolic" Paradise. This project keeps Paradise unpictured; 55:46-78 are readings only. The two seas are a real-world estuary.
